answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted escrow with slow release. To join, an agent must lock real capital that it forfeits if peers catch fake identities. Sybils thus cost linearly: every impostor needs its own funds, so a swarm cannot ride one account. Identities resemble a vine on trellis, each branch paying its own way. Withdrawals pass a guarded jetty, waiting out a challenge window and clawed back if collusion is proven. Honest agents treat deposit as a pearl earned, not cloned.
